title: Lab 233 - Linux Logical Volume Management (LVM) - Advanced

lab_objective.description: The objective of this lab is to practice Linux Logical Volume Management (LVM) by creating a physical volume directly on /dev/sdb, adding it to a volume group, creating multiple logical volumes with different filesystems, and managing their size.
objectives: Create a physical volume directly on /dev/sdb.
Create a volume group and add the physical volume to it.
Create an XFS filesystem on one logical volume.
Create an ext4 filesystem on another logical volume.
Mount the filesystems and configure them for persistent mounting.
Resize the filesystems after extending the logical volumes.
Shrink an ext4 logical volume safely.
Resize the ext4 filesystem before reducing the logical volume.
Save intermediate df -hT output to files for validation.
scenario: You are working as a Linux Systems Administrator for an application server that requires flexible storage management.
A 2 GB disk, /dev/sdb, has been attached to the server. The disk needs to be managed using LVM so that storage can be allocated and resized without having to repartition the disk.
Create a physical volume directly on /dev/sdb and add it to a new volume group named vg_app.
Create two logical volumes in vg_app:
Create an XFS filesystem on lv_data and mount it persistently at /data.
Create an ext4 filesystem on lv_logs and mount it persistently at /logs.
After the initial configuration, increase the size of both logical volumes and resize their respective filesystems.
The ext4 logical volume must then be reduced in size. Because ext4 supports shrinking, safely reduce the filesystem first and then reduce the logical volume.
The XFS filesystem must not be shrunk because XFS does not support shrinking.
Use df -hT at the required stages and save the output to the specified files so that the intermediate storage configuration can be validated.

tasks.title: Identify the New Disk
steps: Identify the newly attached disk and confirm that /dev/sdb is available for use.
The disk /dev/sdb must be used for this lab.
Do not create a partition table or partitions on /dev/sdb.

tasks.title: Create a Physical Volume
steps: Create a physical volume directly on /dev/sdb.
Verify that /dev/sdb is recognized as an LVM physical volume.

tasks.title: Create a Volume Group
steps: Create a volume group named:
vg_app
Add the physical volume /dev/sdb to vg_app.
Verify the volume group and confirm that /dev/sdb is an active physical volume in the volume group.

tasks.title: Create the Data Logical Volume
steps: Create a logical volume named:
lv_data
The logical volume must initially be 600 MB in size.
Verify that lv_data belongs to vg_app and has the required initial size.

tasks.title: Create the Logs Logical Volume
steps: Create a logical volume named:
lv_logs
The logical volume must initially be 500 MB in size.
Verify that lv_logs belongs to vg_app and has the required initial size.

tasks.title: Create the XFS Filesystem
steps: Create an XFS filesystem on:
/dev/vg_app/lv_data
Create the mount point:
/data
Mount the logical volume at /data.
Verify that the filesystem type is XFS and that the filesystem is mounted correctly.

tasks.title: Create the ext4 Filesystem
steps: Create an ext4 filesystem on:
/dev/vg_app/lv_logs
Create the mount point:
/logs
Mount the logical volume at /logs.
Verify that the filesystem type is ext4 and that the filesystem is mounted correctly.

tasks.title: Configure Persistent Mounting
steps: Configure both logical volumes in /etc/fstab so that they are mounted automatically after a system reboot.
The following filesystems must be configured:
/dev/vg_app/lv_data    /data
/dev/vg_app/lv_logs    /logs
Verify the /etc/fstab configuration and confirm that both filesystems can be mounted using the configured entries.

tasks.title: Record the Initial Filesystem Configuration
steps: Run ‘df –hT’ and redirect the output to ‘/home/your_username/lvm_initial’
The file must contain the filesystem information after the initial LVM configuration.

tasks.title: Extend the XFS Logical Volume
steps: Extend lv_data by 200 MB.
The logical volume must increase from approximately 600 MB to approximately 800 MB.
Verify the new logical volume size.

tasks.title: Resize the XFS Filesystem
steps: Resize the XFS filesystem on /data so that it uses the additional space provided to lv_data.
Verify that the filesystem has been successfully expanded.
Run ‘df –hT’ and redirect the output to ‘/home/your_username/lvm_xfs_extend’
The output file must contain the updated filesystem information for /data.

tasks.title: Resize the ext4 Logical Volume
steps: Resize lv_logs from approximately 500 MB to 700 MB.
The logical volume must increase to approximately 700 MB in size.
Verify the new logical volume size.

tasks.title: Resize the ext4 Filesystem
steps: Resize the ext4 filesystem on /logs so that it uses the additional space provided to lv_logs.
Verify that the filesystem has been successfully expanded.
Run ‘df –hT’ and redirect the output to ‘/home/your_username/lvm_ext4_extend’
The output file must contain the updated filesystem information for /logs.

tasks.title: Shrink the ext4 Filesystem and Logical Volume
steps: Safely reduce lv_logs from approximately **700 MB back to 500 MB**.
Before shrinking the filesystem, **unmount /logs**.
Check the ext4 filesystem for errors before performing the resize operation. Using 'e2fsck -f /dev/vg_app/lv_logs'
If there are errors that can be safely repaired, you can use 'e2fsck -f -y /dev/vg_app/lv_logs' otherwise move forward.
Shrink the ext4 filesystem to **500 MB**.
After successfully shrinking the filesystem, reduce the logical volume to **500 MB**.
Mount /logs again after completing the operation.
Verify that the ext4 filesystem and logical volume are approximately **500 MB** in size.
**The filesystem must be reduced before the logical volume is reduced.**

tasks.title: Record the Shrunk Filesystem Configuration
steps: Run ‘df -hT' and redirect the output to ‘/home/your_username/lvm_ext4_shrink’
The output file must contain the filesystem information after shrinking /logs.

tasks.title: Extend the ext4 Logical Volume Again
steps: Extend lv_logs by 200 MB.
The logical volume must increase from approximately 500 MB to approximately 700 MB.
Verify the new logical volume size.

tasks.title: Resize the ext4 Filesystem Again
steps: Resize the ext4 filesystem on /logs so that it uses the additional space.
Verify that the filesystem has successfully grown to approximately 700 MB.

completion_message:
Congratulations!

You have successfully completed Lab 233.

You created and configured an LVM environment using /dev/sdb, created a volume group and multiple logical volumes, worked with both XFS and ext4 filesystems, configured persistent mounts, extended logical volumes, resized filesystems, and safely shrank an ext4 filesystem and logical volume.
